learning_outcomes.text: Develop the basic concepts of Ceramic Materials Science.

Offer students the opportunity to see the applications and possibilities of using these materials in a wide range of applications, ranging from classical applications of everyday life to advanced state-of-the-art applications, such as sensors and spacecraft units.
Teach characterization and analysis techniques, which are important for the student in the industry, both in the product line and in the field of development research.
Familiarize students with ceramic materials and glasses.
Consolidate the structural mechanisms for the creation of ceramic materials and glasses with defined properties.
Use this knowledge to properly apply ceramic materials and glasses in various fields.
Search, analyze and synthesize data and information using the necessary technologies.
Promote free, creative and inductive thinking.

syllabus_topics: Definition, properties, and applications of ceramic materials (sintered polycrystalline, glasses, glass-ceramics, monocrystalline and natural ceramics)

assessment_methods.method: Final written examination (combination of multiple-choice questions and developing topics)
Presentation of a topic related to ceramics

assessment_rules: Students are evaluated by a final written examination in Greek that includes a combination of multiple-choice questions and developing topics, and a presentation of a topic related to ceramics. Students have the right to view their exam scripts after the grading results are published and to ask questions.
bibliography: Barsoum M., Fundamentals of Ceramics, 2003 Institute of Physics Publishing Bristol and Philadelphia
Ftikos C. (2005). Ceramics Science and Technique, NTUA University Publications
Vatalis A. (2008) Material Science and Technology, Ziti Publications
degree: Materials Science and Engineering — Πτυχίο Τμήματος Επιστήμης και Μηχανικής Υλικών (first cycle, 240 ECTS, curriculum ΕΜΥ)
